target_customer: Small and mid-size advertisers (targeting those spending $20,000 to $1 million per month, mostly under $100,000) running Facebook and other paid social campaigns
problem: Running and optimising paid social campaigns took many hours a week. Kuhcoon, later Automate Ads, set up and optimised campaigns from a goal, a budget and creative assets.
business_model: SaaS for advertisers, likely a fee tied to ad spend (the source does not state pricing)

founders.name: Andrew Torba
founders.background_notes: Wikipedia says he was CEO from October 2011 until August 2016 and was a college roommate of his co-founder; the school is not named.

founders.name: Charles Szymanski
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CTO in TechCrunch (Feb 2015) and Wikipedia. The YC page lists no founders.

competitors.what: full-automation ad management for very large advertisers

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with the Facebook ads API and running automated rotation and optimisation across audience segments is standard but nontrivial engineering, with Google AdWords and other networks planned.

defensibility.rationale: Ad automation sat on top of platform APIs and larger vendors already automated for big advertisers. The main edge was a one-ad-per-segment rotation method and a self-serve small-business focus.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source reports an incumbent copying it. The company nearly shut down before AdHawk, a competitor, bought its technology in October 2017 with no staff moving over.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Feb 2015) reports the company claimed more than 6,000 advertisers in 90+ countries and average savings of 40% of ad spend, which indicates early adoption among small advertisers, though the figures are company claims.

branding.domain_note: Launched at kuhcoon.com; later used automateads.com (seen in a database listing).

brand_strength.rationale: The invented name Kuhcoon was hard to spell and the company switched to a descriptive name within months of the YC batch, which suggests the original name did not serve it. No community or brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Kuhcoon, renamed Automate Ads on 25 June 2015, automated Facebook ad campaigns for small advertisers and reported 6,000 advertisers by February 2015. Reported YC funding was about $120K and no later round was found. It nearly shut down and AdHawk bought the technology in October 2017 for an undisclosed price without taking staff, so the exit was a soft landing, but no source states the cause in the taxonomy's terms.
